title: Testing Your Code: assert and pytest
concepts: test files and test functions (test_ prefix)
comparing decimals with round() and pytest.approx()
breaking code on purpose to check tests

ai_pair_moment.flaw: Asked for tests that catch any mistake in boxes_needed(), the AI wrote three tests that all pass on Asha's module. On a broken copy that uses round() they still all pass: the 24-biscuit test divides exactly, and the 0-biscuit test has no assert at all. The improved file tests 40 and 13 biscuits too, and two of its tests fail on the broken copy, as they should.

changes: pytest is a third-party package. The lesson installs it with `python -m pip install -U pytest` and points to Chapter 24 for packages in depth; virtual environments are left for that chapter.

Tool change: a Python example with a `.pytest` sidecar file is run with `python -m pytest <options from the sidecar> <file>` at a fixed width of 56 columns, and the run time in pytest's summary line is ignored when outputs are compared. tools/setup_check.py installs pytest into every Python toolchain. STANDARDS.md section 6 documents the sidecar.

Broken copies live in their own folders with copies of the tests, so learners can see a test fail without changing the working module: examples/broken for Steps 4 and 5, and examples/ai/broken and examples/ai/broken2 for the AI section, which works on the finished module with the USD rule. examples/testfirst holds the module before the USD change, examples/usd shows the old Step 3 test failing after it, and examples/final holds the finished module and tests.
unittest and pytest fixtures are left out to keep the chapter to assert, plain test functions and approx.
outstanding_issues: pytest's separator lines stretch to the width of the terminal; the lesson's outputs use a fixed width of 56 columns, so lines of = and _ on a learner's screen are longer.
The run time in pytest's last line changes on every run; the lesson shows 0.01s.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
